title: VPC Traffic Governor Terraform module: modular security groups, NACLs, private DNS views, and egress policies
creator: Aisha Navarro
description: Deliver a reusable Terraform module (vpc-traffic-governor) that centralizes VPC security controls for Private deployments. The module should provide opinionated, composable defaults for security groups and NACLs, a configurable split-horizon private DNS view for service discovery, and a pluggable egress policy engine (allowlist, proxy redirect, and deny-by-default modes). This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, upgrade/migration scripts, and integration with our module registry and CI gating.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Module generates deterministic plans with default settings for new VPCs and can be consumed by existing on-prem/private stacks. 2) Module provides a clear upgrade path (0.x -> 1.x) with automated terraform state migration scripts and a migration plan document. 3) Egress policy modes (allowlist, proxy, deny-default) are unit-tested and validated in staging via synthetic traffic. 4) Private DNS split-horizon can be enabled per-environment and preserves records across upgrades. 5) CI checks include plan-diff guardrails, terraform-compliance tests, and a canary apply stage. 6) Security review signoff and perf baseline (no >5% latency regression on control-plane operations).
implementation_notes:
- Directory: modules/vpc-traffic-governor
- Inputs: vpc_id, environment_tag, subnets_map, allowed_egress_cidrs, egress_mode (allowlist|proxy|deny), proxy_endpoint, private_dns_zones
- Outputs: security_group_ids, nacl_ids, private_dns_view_ids, egress_policy_id, migration_guidance
- Use policy-as-code (OPA/Rego) hooks for validate-only checks in CI
- Provide an upgrade helper script (tfmigrate + state-backup) and a terraform lockfile to force known-good provider versions
- Keep resources modular so customers can opt-out of NACLs or DNS handling without forking
- Include example consumption manifests for hosted, dedicated, and on-prem variants
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module to registry-canary branch. 2) Publish v1.0.0-canary to internal registry. 3) Run automated canary apply in a non-prod tenant (runbook step: snapshot state, apply, smoke tests). 4) Monitor VPC Flow Logs, reachability checks, and console telemetry for 48h. 5) If stable, promote to v1.0.0 and schedule staged rollout to low-risk customers. 6) Offer manual migration support for enterprise customers on older module versions.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests with terratest for SG/NACL combinations
- Integration tests deploying to ephemeral staging VPCs with different egress modes
- Terraform-compliance scenarios for deny-default drift detection
- End-to-end smoke tests: DNS resolution of private zones, egress path verification using curl proxies, and VPC reachability checks
- Load test for control-plane applying many module instances to measure plan/apply latency
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: State migration may break existing references to SG/NACL IDs. Mitigation: Provide tfmigrate steps that create aliases and update remote-state references; add preflight check to detect cross-stack references.
Risk: Egress deny-default could block management agents during rollout. Mitigation: Default allowlist includes management CIDRs and agent endpoints; require explicit opt-in to strict deny mode.
Risk: Private DNS reconciliation could overwrite customer custom records. Mitigation: Module uses separate private DNS view and does not delete records outside its managed set; document the behavior clearly.
migration_steps: 1) Run ./scripts/backup-state.sh <workspace>. 2) Run ./scripts/tfmigrate-stage.sh to import existing SG/NACL resources into new module namespace (dry-run first). 3) Apply canary in staging and validate. 4) Run ./scripts/replace-references.sh to update dependent stacks' outputs. 5) Promote module after successful verification.
